title: Row headers should apply to all cells in the row
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

Regarding the behaviour of row headers, the [specification](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/tables.html#the-th-element) states that:
> The [row] header cell applies to some of the subsequent cells in the same row(s).

This seems like a particularly limiting decision, as this would prevent table's with re-orderable columns or tables that have an actions column as the first column (both which are common practices), from ever working correctly without some work-around. I wondered if this issue may be due to the patterns that I mentioned not being prevalent during the creation of the specification.

For people using screen readers, this behaviour can result in particularly poor results, especially in the use cases that I referred to earlier. As a result of the row header only applying to subsequent cells, you don't have sufficient context on earlier columns, to understand what the cells might relate to. Therefore, you may have to manually add in context with something like ARIA or visually hidden text.

As a result, I would recommend that this is changed to:
> The [row] header cell applies to all other cells in the same row(s).

I hope that I have filed this correctly, but apologise in advance if I have not - this is my first time opening an issue on this repo. Please let me know if any changes are required! Thank you 😄
